title: Introduce micro-changelog shards and sample-input scrubbing for safer, composable release notes
author: Leah Kim
description: Motivation: Onboarding new model variants produces long release notes that mix perf deltas, dataset examples, and occasional sensitive sample artefacts. This PR introduces: 1) micro-changelog shards: compact per-variant changelog fragments with stable shard IDs that can be composed into release bundles; each shard records metadata (variant, profile hash, sample-anchors, diff-summary) and a lightweight digital signature for provenance. 2) sample-input scrubbing stage: a pluggable pipeline that canonicalizes example inputs, strips or masks detected PII, and maps samples to privacy-safe tokens that still allow QA to reproduce behavioral regressions. 3) release-note assembler hooks: heuristics to automatically assemble full release notes from selected shards, prioritizing perf regressions/improvements, breaking changes, and curated examples. The description field below outlines scope, data migration, testing, and rollout plan. Scope and API: A new micro_changelog module exposes: - create_shard(variant_id, profile_hash, changes_summary, example_samples, tags) -> shard_id - sign_shard(shard_id, signer_key) -> signature - scrub_samples(raw_samples, policy) -> scrubbed_samples, mapping_map - assemble_release(shard_ids[], policy) -> release_blob The shard schema is compact JSON (max ~2KB) and intentionally avoids embedding raw inputs in favor of scrubbed tokens or guarded sample references. Data migration: we backfilled shards for the last 90 days of model releases using a best-effort sampler and a conservative scrub policy (remove free-text email/phone/SSN, hash long GUIDs). Backfill script is included as tools/backfill/micro_changelog_backfill.py and executed during the migration step. Rollout plan: default behavior is opt-in for existing onboarding flows. The registry CLI gains a flag (--emit-micro-changelog) and the onboarding CI job will validate shard signatures. After 2 weeks of opt-in telemetry we'll flip the default to on if no major issues occur. Security considerations: scrubbing relies on a layered approach: regex detectors, token classification model (small on-device), and a manual allowlist for curated examples. Scrubbed mappings are encrypted at rest and only exposed to authorized reviewers via the registry console. Implementation notes: - New DB table micro_changelog_shards (shard_id PK, variant_id, profile_hash, payload, signature, created_by, created_at) with a TTL and compact index on profile_hash. - Signer integration hooks for KMS (abstracted interface, default no-op in dev). - CLI and REST API endpoints for shard lifecycle (create/list/get/assemble). Tests and CI: added unit tests covering scrubbing rules (tests/test_sample_scrubber.py), shard serialization/deserialization (tests/test_shard_roundtrip.py), and assembler heuristics (tests/test_assemble_priority.py). Added an integration test that runs a small onboarding flow and asserts the assembled release contains exactly one perf-delta entry for a synthetic variant. Migration note: DB migration script included in migrations/0028_add_micro_changelog_shards.sql. Backfill includes rate-limiting and idempotency. Related work: builds on the profiling and release-assembly effort in ENG-4022 but avoids embedding raw samples which previously caused privacy incidents. Drawbacks and limits: scrubber is conservative and may remove contextual tokens used in rare prompts; we include an approval flow to pin curated examples when automatic scrubbing is too aggressive. Next steps: wire shard visibility into the Console release UI and add opt-out tooling for enterprise customers.
commits: 3 commits: (a) add micro_changelog core module, DB schema, and migration; (b) add sample scrubber and CLI flags; (c) backfill script, tests, and docs updates

release_notes: - Added micro-changelog shards: compact per-variant change fragments to power automated release notes and diffs. - Added sample-input scrubbing pipeline to remove PII from onboarding examples and preserve privacy-safe mappings. - CLI flag --emit-micro-changelog to opt into shard emission; default will flip to on after an opt-in window. See docs/changes/micro-changelog.md for details.
